newsitem.title: UK: Energis launches assault on telephone prices.
newsitem.headline: Energis launches assault on telephone prices.

text.p: Energis, the fledgling telecoms group owned by the National Grid Group Plc, sparked a call price battle on Tuesday, slashing international charges to the five most popular destinations from the UK.

As well as price cuts to 200 other destinations, telephone calls to the Netherlands, Ireland, Germany, France and the U.S will all now cost 10 pence per minute -- beating British Telecommunications Plc's similar charges by up to 42 percent, Energis said.

Eight weeks after winning an international licence, Energis said it was launching its first real assault on the international telephone call duopoly between British Telecommunications and Cable and Wireless Plc's Mercury unit.

Energis, which supplies telecoms services to about 14,000 business customers via the Grid's high voltage electricity pylons, said the cuts were part of its new international call package called World Link.

Comparing its rates to BT's Business Choice 2 international direct dial package, Energis said firms signing up to World Link would save up to 42 percent from February 24 -- but pay a higher fee to join.

Per minute calls to Denmark, Sweden and Switzerland have been cut to 14 pence; to Australia, Finland and New Zealand they now cost 20 pence; to Hong Kong and Singapore 30 pence and to Japan 35 pence, Energis said.

Energis said its new rates were the lowest ever permanent published charges offered by a UK telecom firm. With a dramatically reduced cost base, Energis says it has every incentive to be aggressive on price to grow its market share.

Dominant carrier BT has cut its international telephone prices by almost 170 million pounds in just five months as rivals try to muscle in on its vast market share and world telecom markets are eased open.
In a battle to maintain margins as telephone prices are set to plunge, BT last week cut the costs of calls to 33 destinations by between 10 and 37 percent.
But Energis dismissed BT's cuts saying it had also cut its international base rates to more than 200 destinations.
Energis charges 16 stg per month for its World Link package. BT's Business Choices 2 costs 15 stg per quarter, giving a 28 percent discount off foreign calls.

With an international licence safely under its belt, Energis no longer has to lease line capacity from BT or Mercury at artificially high prices. It can now buy permanent capacity from operators -- and save money.
Another key way to reduce cost bases further is via "correspondent agreements" with other telecoms players to end each other's calls at the lowest prices possible.
Energis's chief executive Mike Grabiner told Reuters in January that the group wanted a relationship with players such as Deutsche Telekom AG and France Telecom so it can cut costs and prices.
While no details are yet forthcoming, he said at the time that Energis was near closing deals -- likely to be correspondent agreements -- with "a number of European operators".
Energis has already signed correspondent agreements with America's Sprint and PTT Telecom in the Netherlands.
